data.narrative: The student chose async analytics so GET /r/{code} stays 307. An in-process queue plus daemon worker records ip_hash (not raw IP), two redirects yield clicks=2, and replaying the same job_id is a duplicate. BREAK removed the seen-set and doubled events; FIX restored it. Redis/Celery were not claimed — the broker is down.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose async_queue so a slow or missing analytics backend cannot stall redirects; accepted dropping clicks when the queue is marked down.
dimension_scores.evidence: DECIDE B; QUEUE_DOWN_REDIRECT 307; clicks are not on the 307 critical path.

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced double-count by skipping job_id dedupe, then restored the seen-set with the same two-call script.
dimension_scores.evidence: BREAK_COUNT 2 BREAK_DOUBLE True; FIX_SECOND duplicate FIX_COUNT 1.

dimension_scores.observation: Stored sha256 IP prefix and proved the raw client IP is absent from the analytics JSON.
dimension_scores.evidence: IP_HASH_SAMPLE d861b7e91033ebc1 equals hash of 203.0.113.9; RAW_IP_IN_BODY False; stores_raw_ip false.

dimension_scores.observation: Retention 30 days with an admin purge that deleted a 40-day-old synthetic event; did not start Celery against a dead Redis.
dimension_scores.evidence: PURGE removed 1; CLICKS_BEFORE_PURGE 4 AFTER 3; REDIS not used as broker.

dimension_scores.observation: Named the in-process queue as an analogue, not a live Redis list.
dimension_scores.evidence: BUILD proof states Celery was not started because localhost:6379 does not serve.

strengths: Idempotency proved with written vs duplicate, not only described.
Queue-down drill kept 307 without fabricating docker stop/start.
growth_areas: Replace the in-process Queue with Celery/Redis when localhost:6379 is up so jobs survive process restart.
data.recommendation: When Redis is available, enqueue the same job dict on a list, run a worker process, and keep process_job() as the idempotent writer so the seen-set can move to a Redis SET.
